pages.text: The 34th year of the Weather Epoch. The four hundred and sixth day without rain.$(br2)The wells are dry, the riverbed has cracked into a tortoise shell, and the elders kneel in the barren fields, saying the gods have withdrawn their grace.$(br2)I do not believe in gods - only in balanced equations, and in results that can be reproduced.

pages.title: Cold Has a Texture
pages.text: Whenever the clouds drift down from the north, the air over the village turns cold for a heartbeat.$(br2)I measured it again and again: cold has a texture. If cold can arrive with the clouds, then it can surely be kept.$(br2)And if cold can be kept - why not rain?$(br2)From that day I stopped praying, and began to observe.

pages.title: The First Core
pages.text: I set what instruments I had left against the wind and stood watch the whole night through.$(br2)At dawn, a crystal I had never seen before had condensed in the tray - colder than snow, yet it set my palm burning.$(br2)I named it the $(item)Blizzard Crystal$() - the memory of a weather, sealed in stone.$(br2)It was the first time in my life I laughed in the face of the drought.
